milestones.title: Tehran attested as a village near Rayy
milestones.detail: The scholar Muhammad b. Hammad al-Tihrani al-Razi, a native of the village, died in 874, which shows it already existed. The first surviving text to name Tehran, Ibn al-Balkhi's Fars-nama, was written before 1116 and praises its pomegranates.
milestones.source: Encyclopaedia of Islam, 2nd ed., vol. X (Brill, 2000), s.v. 'Tihran' (V. Minorsky, C.E. Bosworth, J. Calmard, B. Hourcade), pp. 482-496, https://bahai-library.com/pdf/e/encyclopedia_islam_tihran.pdf

milestones.title: Yaqut describes Tehran on the eve of the Mongol invasion
milestones.detail: The geographer Yaqut, who visited just before the Mongol invasion, described a considerable town of 12 quarters with underground houses and dense gardens. The neighbouring city of Rayy was ruined by the Mongols and never recovered.
milestones.source: Encyclopaedia of Islam, 2nd ed., vol. X (Brill, 2000), s.v. 'Tihran' (V. Minorsky, C.E. Bosworth, J. Calmard, B. Hourcade), pp. 482-496, https://bahai-library.com/pdf/e/encyclopedia_islam_tihran.pdf ; Encyclopaedia Britannica (1911), 'Teheran', https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/1911_Encyclop%C3%A6dia_Britannica/Teheran_(city)

milestones.title: Clavijo finds an unwalled town
milestones.detail: The Castilian ambassador Ruy Gonzalez de Clavijo, the first European visitor, stayed in Tehran on 6 July 1404. It had no walls, and nearby Rayy was uninhabited.
milestones.source: Encyclopaedia of Islam, 2nd ed., vol. X (Brill, 2000), s.v. 'Tihran' (V. Minorsky, C.E. Bosworth, J. Calmard, B. Hourcade), pp. 482-496, https://bahai-library.com/pdf/e/encyclopedia_islam_tihran.pdf

milestones.title: Shah Tahmasp I builds a bazaar and town wall
milestones.detail: The Safavid shah gave Tehran a bazaar and a wall about one farsakh long with four gates and 114 towers, one for each sura of the Quran. The town's prosperity dates from this point.
milestones.source: Encyclopaedia of Islam, 2nd ed., vol. X (Brill, 2000), s.v. 'Tihran' (V. Minorsky, C.E. Bosworth, J. Calmard, B. Hourcade), pp. 482-496, https://bahai-library.com/pdf/e/encyclopedia_islam_tihran.pdf

milestones.title: Agha Mohammad Khan makes Tehran his capital
milestones.detail: The founder of the Qajar dynasty chose the hitherto undistinguished town as capital in 1786. Ten years later it still had fewer than 15,000 people.
milestones.source: Encyclopaedia of Islam, 2nd ed., vol. X (Brill, 2000), s.v. 'Tihran' (V. Minorsky, C.E. Bosworth, J. Calmard, B. Hourcade), pp. 482-496, https://bahai-library.com/pdf/e/encyclopedia_islam_tihran.pdf

milestones.title: Cholera epidemic
milestones.detail: Cholera had afflicted Tehran since 1823. The diplomat Arthur de Gobineau reckoned that one-third of the inhabitants died of it in 1856.
milestones.source: Encyclopaedia of Islam, 2nd ed., vol. X (Brill, 2000), s.v. 'Tihran' (V. Minorsky, C.E. Bosworth, J. Calmard, B. Hourcade), pp. 482-496, https://bahai-library.com/pdf/e/encyclopedia_islam_tihran.pdf

milestones.title: Naser al-Din Shah orders the old walls demolished
milestones.detail: The decision was taken in December 1867. A new octagonal rampart and ditch with twelve gates, designed on Vauban's system, was built over about four years and enclosed several times the old area.
milestones.source: Encyclopaedia of Islam, 2nd ed., vol. X (Brill, 2000), s.v. 'Tihran' (V. Minorsky, C.E. Bosworth, J. Calmard, B. Hourcade), pp. 482-496, https://bahai-library.com/pdf/e/encyclopedia_islam_tihran.pdf ; Encyclopaedia Britannica (1911), 'Teheran', https://en.wikisource.org/wiki/1911_Encyclop%C3%A6dia_Britannica/Teheran_(city)

milestones.title: Tehran-Rey railway opens
milestones.detail: A metre-gauge line 5.5 miles long linked Tehran to the shrine town of Shah Abdol-Azim (Rey). In 1911 it was still the only railway in Persia.

milestones.title: Constitutional Revolution
milestones.detail: The shah proclaimed a constitutional monarchy in August 1906 and the first parliament met at Baharestan. A municipal law followed in 1907.

milestones.title: Street-widening law reshapes the city
milestones.detail: Under Reza Shah, a 1933 law drove straight avenues through the old fabric and along the line of the walls. The twelve Qajar gates, most of the Arg palaces and the Takyeh Dowlat were demolished.
milestones.source: Encyclopaedia of Islam, 2nd ed., vol. X (Brill, 2000), s.v. 'Tihran' (V. Minorsky, C.E. Bosworth, J. Calmard, B. Hourcade), pp. 482-496, https://bahai-library.com/pdf/e/encyclopedia_islam_tihran.pdf

milestones.title: University of Tehran founded
milestones.detail: The foundation stone of the university was laid in 1935 on the new avenue that marked the northern edge of the city.
milestones.source: Encyclopaedia of Islam, 2nd ed., vol. X (Brill, 2000), s.v. 'Tihran' (V. Minorsky, C.E. Bosworth, J. Calmard, B. Hourcade), pp. 482-496, https://bahai-library.com/pdf/e/encyclopedia_islam_tihran.pdf

milestones.title: Railway station built
milestones.detail: The railway and its station, built in 1938, came to mark the southern edge of Reza Shah's city.
milestones.source: Encyclopaedia of Islam, 2nd ed., vol. X (Brill, 2000), s.v. 'Tihran' (V. Minorsky, C.E. Bosworth, J. Calmard, B. Hourcade), pp. 482-496, https://bahai-library.com/pdf/e/encyclopedia_islam_tihran.pdf

milestones.title: First comprehensive plan
milestones.detail: The Gruen and Farmanfarmaian master plan set the city limits for 25 years and steered growth west along the foothills towards Karaj.
milestones.source: Encyclopaedia of Islam, 2nd ed., vol. X (Brill, 2000), s.v. 'Tihran' (V. Minorsky, C.E. Bosworth, J. Calmard, B. Hourcade), pp. 482-496, https://bahai-library.com/pdf/e/encyclopedia_islam_tihran.pdf

milestones.title: Azadi (Shahyad) Tower completed
milestones.detail: The marble-clad tower was commissioned by the Shah to mark 2,500 years of the Persian monarchy and opened in January 1972.

milestones.title: Iranian Revolution
milestones.detail: The revolution of 1979 ended the monarchy. Informal housing spread on the city's edges and was legalised in 1982, and the planned Shahestan Pahlavi centre and the metro were shelved.
milestones.source: Encyclopaedia of Islam, 2nd ed., vol. X (Brill, 2000), s.v. 'Tihran' (V. Minorsky, C.E. Bosworth, J. Calmard, B. Hourcade), pp. 482-496, https://bahai-library.com/pdf/e/encyclopedia_islam_tihran.pdf

milestones.title: Tehran Metro begins operation
milestones.detail: The suburban Line 5 to Karaj opened on 7 March 1999, and Lines 1 and 2 entered commercial service from 2000.

milestones.title: Milad Tower completed
milestones.detail: The 435 m telecommunications tower, begun in 1997, became the tallest structure in Iran.

notes: Start date: Tehran has no founding event. It grew from a village in the orbit of the ancient city of Rayy (Rhages), whose ruins lie inside today's metropolis and whose site has been settled for several thousand years; Rayy is a different city and is not used as the start. The Encyclopaedia of Islam says it is uncertain when the name first appears: the earliest surviving text is Ibn al-Balkhi's Fars-nama (before 1116), but al-Sam'ani records a native of the village who died in 874, so the village existed by then. 874 is therefore used as the start and marked 'estimated'; a stricter reading would start at about 1116. Britannica (1911) cites Yaqut (1224) as the earliest description. Population: there is no figure before 1628, and nothing for the village and small town of 874-1554. 19th-century figures are travellers' estimates and are strongly seasonal (the court and much of the population left in summer), so winter and summer figures are labelled. The first Tehran 'census' (Abd al-Ghaffar, 1868) yielded an estimate of 155,736, and Britannica (1911) gives about 280,000 for c. 1910; the Encyclopaedia of Islam calls the period's figures unreliable and prefers Zandjani's series (106,482 in 1883, 160,000 in 1891, 210,000 in 1922, 310,000 in 1932), which is used here, so the 1868 and 1910 figures are left out rather than shown as a rise and fall. Chandler gives 70,000 for 1850, 150,000 for 1900 and 243,000 for 1925, also left out in favour of the Zandjani series. Britannica (1911) says the Afghans destroyed almost the whole town in 1723; no population figure exists for that collapse. Landmarks: the Skyscraper Center does not list Milad Tower in its Tehran building table, so its height is from Wikipedia. Toghrol Tower in Rey (20 m) is omitted because no completion year could be sourced; heights could not be sourced for the Shah (Imam) Mosque, the old Plasco Building (1962, collapsed 2017), Azadi Stadium, Tabiat Bridge or the Bank Markazi Tower. The Khomeini mausoleum (91 m minarets) and the Grand Mosalla (135 m minarets) are omitted because they have no clear completion year. Wikipedia reports war damage to Tehran in 2025-26; this could not be checked against primary sources and is not recorded as a milestone.
